title: Holmes 2020 · Exploratory sound-type acquisition
citation: Holmes, N. P., Martin, D. J., Mitchell, W., Noorani, Z., & Thorne, A. (2020). Do sounds near the hand facilitate tactile reaction times? Four experiments and a meta-analysis provide mixed support and suggest a small effect size. Experimental Brain Research, 238, 995–1009.
notes: Published study settings are available for inspection. See the source-backed method and remaining execution requirements.

reference_parameters.planner_scope: The source settings describe this companion procedure. The Planner contains no executable trial schedule for it.

published_method.scope: Exploratory ExperimentX labelled E4 in the code. The journal's Experiment 4 driving task is E5 in the archive.
published_method.design: The exploratory acquisition was intended to compare different auditory waveform types and distances in the near/far task. The paper excludes it after discovering that the auditory type and location codes were confounded.
published_method.timing: The archived routine uses the hand-task DAQ and tactile/vocal routes with a nominal 2.5 s acquisition buffer. The archived material includes both 40- and 48-trial blocks; this does not resolve a valid common analysis schedule.
published_method.outcome: Only inspect the historical design and staging. The coded sound contrast cannot support an independent causal PPS estimate.

stimulus_type.gap: Planned independent sound-by-distance comparison is impossible because each sound type appears at just one distance.

value.method: Align the near audio and tactile slices at sample 800 and far audio at sample 777 with tactile at sample 800, zero-based at 8000 Hz. Rescale audio by the archived tactile level divided by the speaker gain. All pairs matched to numerical precision.
value.consequence: The manipulation coupled tactile waveform with auditory type and distance.

implementation_gaps: The intended comparison cannot be recovered from confounded sound-type and distance labels. Reproducing the archived procedure requires the original waveform routing and validation of audible condition identities.
Distinct archived protocol versions, participant-level assignment and original retained analysis scope remain unresolved.
